note: The 2026-09-20 seed population. Each (condition, seed) is its OWN `boltz predict` invocation, because boltz 2.2.1 calls `seed_everything(seed)` once per invocation and batching several inputs would make one input's sampling depend on the previous one's. The MSA is never fetched: every input names the 2026-09-19 run's own emitted csv by path, so the MSA is byte-identical across the whole population and the only difference between two runs of one condition is the seed.

workstation.note: an unrelated user process (a game) held 5,165 MiB of the device throughout; every run still fit

ion_syntax.yaml: sequences: - ligand: {id: [C, D, E], ccd: ZN}
ion_syntax.no_constraint_supplied: no `pocket` and no `contact` constraint was given, so where the three ions went is the predictor's own statement
ion_syntax.intake_consequence: boltz writes an ion as a HETATM row whose _atom_site.label_seq_id is `.`; physical_intake::mmcif requires an integer there, so each zinc prediction is staged to a `-protein.cif` carrying its ATOM rows verbatim before the library reads it

determinism_receipt: the 2026-09-20 `complex` seed-0 run reproduces the 2026-09-19 `binder-target` seed-0 run's 204 alpha-carbon coordinate tokens exactly, although one was driven by a FASTA input and the other by a YAML input
